Apptronik's most important audiences — the executives, customers, investors, and partners who will define how the world sees Apollo — encounter our technology through live demonstrations. This role is responsible for making those moments exceptional.
As
Senior Application Engineer, Customer Experience
, you will own the full lifecycle of Apollo demonstrations at our California office and at events worldwide. You will design, build, and operate the robot behaviors and workcell environments that bring Apollo to life for VIP visitors — applying the same engineering discipline, rigor, and process we use for every customer field deployment.
Operating as the senior technical presence at our California satellite office, you will work with significant autonomy, represent Apptronik's engineering capability to our most critical audiences, and serve as a direct feedback channel between what customers experience and what our product teams build. This is a high-visibility, high-impact engineering role at the intersection of robotics, customer engagement, and product storytelling.
This role is part of the Applications Engineering team and operates under the same processes, standards, and expectations as every other Application Engineer. The California office is a flagship environment where Apptronik's capabilities are on display to the world's most important audiences, and this engineer plays a central role in shaping those experiences.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Requirements & Strategy
Stakeholder alignment —
Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership to define objectives, success criteria, and technical scope for each high-priority visit; capture the agreed storyline and constraints in a concise brief that aligns all internal stakeholders before execution begins.
Technical scoping authority —
Serve as the definitive technical voice on Apollo's demonstrable capabilities — providing honest, confident assessments of what can be shown credibly and reliably to any given audience, and shaping stakeholder expectations accordingly.
Audience-driven design —
Translate visit objectives into scenario designs that reflect real customer problems and workflows, ensuring every demonstration is grounded in the customer's world, not just the robot's capabilities.
Design & Architecture
Solution architecture —
Design demonstration scenarios with the same structured approach used in customer field deployments: clear requirements, defined success criteria, risk assessment, and a documented architecture that can be handed off and reproduced.
Fallback and risk design —
Define comprehensive fallback architectures and failure-mode mitigation strategies that protect demonstration integrity under live conditions — anticipating failure paths before they occur and building recovery into the run-of-show by design.
Simulation-driven development —
Build and maintain demonstration-specific simulation environments using tools such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Gazebo, or MuJoCo to validate and optimize robot behaviors before live deployment, reducing integration risk and rehearsal time.
Build & Integration
Application development —
Develop, configure, and tune the demo applications and robot behaviors required for each scenario, reusing production-grade software where possible and building purpose-built variants where needed — maintaining code quality and documentation standards throughout.
Workcell ownership —
Build and own the Apollo demonstration environment at the California office — including hardware configuration and staging — ensuring the environment meets both technical requirements and the experiential standards expected by VIP visitors.
Hardening and readiness —
Drive demonstration readiness through rigorous rehearsal, systematic testing, and issue tracking; identify hardware and software problems early and maintain accountability for their resolution with the relevant engineering teams.
Execution
Run-of-show ownership —
Own every aspect of live demonstration execution: pre-flight checks, real-time robot operation, presenter support, and calm, decisive triage and recovery when issues arise. Perform consistently under the highest-stakes conditions this company faces.
Guest engagement —
Support presenters and engage directly with visitors as needed during live events — answering technical questions clearly, adapting to audience interest in real time, and ensuring every guest interaction reflects well on Apptronik. Leadership and C-suite will typically lead formal presentations for VIP visits.
Post-demonstration review —
Lead structured post-demonstration reviews to capture outcomes, failures, and follow-up actions; translate findings into concrete feedback for engineering and product teams to inform platform and capability development.
Event support —
Lead or support demonstrations at trade shows, industry events, and customer sites. From time to time, may be asked to lead high-profile demonstrations at Apptronik HQ in Austin. Approximately 20–40% travel is required domestically and internationally.
Program Management & Enablement
Concurrent program ownership —
Manage multiple demonstration requests in parallel — owning scope, timeline, rehearsal planning, and resource coordination across concurrent visits and events with minimal supervision.
Enablement assets —
Build and maintain comprehensive runbooks, SOPs, checklists, and software tools that enable trained colleagues and partners to execute standard demonstrations consistently and independently.
Product feedback loop —
Serve as a direct conduit between live customer experience and internal product development — systematically capturing what resonates, what fails, and what customers ask for, and ensuring that intelligence reaches the teams who can act on it.

Company Overview
At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.
Position Overview
We're looking for a hands-on, highly technical Robotics Application Engineer to work on the software that bridges our foundation models and real-world deployment. This role sits at the intersection of software development, systems integration, and operations — requiring a blend of technical depth and creative problem-solving. You'll translate complex real-world requirements into robust, deployable robotic solutions and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver and continuously improve them.
Responsibilities
Design, develop, and deploy software for robotic systems, including programming, configuration, and validation.
Integrate and deploy robotic software solutions into production environments.
Test, troubleshoot, and debug robotic applications — tracing failures across hardware, software, and model layers.
Work closely with ML and core robotics engineers to surface deployment failures, reproduce edge cases, and translate field learnings into system improvements.
Analyze and improve robot algorithms and system performance over time.
Build and maintain technical documentation, runbooks, and tooling to support configuration, monitoring, and performance evaluation.
Collaborate with hardware, operations, and R&D teams to optimize robotic performance and scalability.
Preferred Qualifications
BS, MS, or higher degree in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
3–5+ years of hands-on experience in robotics application development, system integration, or field deployment.
Proficiency in Python and C++; strong working knowledge of ROS/ROS2.
Familiarity with AI and machine learning techniques as applied to robotic systems.
Background in autonomous systems — robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, industrial automation, or similar.
Familiarity with vision systems, simulation tools, and sensor integration.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

About Field AI
Field AI is building the future of embodied intelligence. Our autonomy software enables robots to operate safely and effectively in complex, dynamic environments across industries such as energy, manufacturing, construction, mining, and logistics.
We work closely with some of the world’s largest industrial organizations to deploy advanced robotic systems that solve meaningful, real-world challenges.
The Role
Field AI is seeking a Manager, Field Operations within our Industrials vertical to lead and scale our growing team of Field Applications Engineers. This team sits at the intersection of our customers, robotic platforms, autonomy software, and product development teams. It is responsible for successful field deployments and ensuring our technology delivers measurable value in demanding operational environments.
In this role, you will manage the strategic direction, day-to-day performance, and development of our Field Applications Engineering team while building the operational processes, organizational structure, and global capabilities needed to support Field AI’s continued growth. You will oversee customer deployments from technical preparation through field execution, help allocate resources across competing priorities, and establish consistent standards for operational readiness, safety, quality, and customer communication.
The ideal candidate combines strong people leadership with hands-on technical judgment and field operations experience. You are comfortable working directly with Forward Deployed engineers, Field Application Engineers, Technical leads and customer stakeholders and you know how to create structure in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
Responsibilities
Lead, coach, and develop a team of Field Applications Engineers responsible for deploying and supporting Field AI’s technology at customer sites.
Scale the Field Applications Engineering organization to support an expanding portfolio of customers, robotic platforms, applications, and geographic regions.
Establish clear team roles, performance expectations, career paths, training programs, and technical competency standards.
Recruit, onboard, and develop new Field Applications Engineers as the organization grows globally.
Plan staffing and allocate field engineering resources across customer deployments, demonstrations, pilots, and production programs.
Ensure deployments are properly scoped, staffed, documented, and prepared before teams arrive at customer sites.
Develop repeatable processes, playbooks, tools, and operating standards for deployment readiness, commissioning, testing, troubleshooting, customer acceptance, and ongoing support.
Partner with customers to understand their workflows, technical environments, operational requirements, safety standards, and success criteria.
Serve as an escalation point for complex technical, operational, and customer-facing issues during deployments.
Work closely with Product, Engineering, Program Management, Sales, Solutions, and Customer Success teams to ensure alignment throughout the customer lifecycle.
Create effective feedback loops between field teams and product development teams, translating deployment insights into actionable product and engineering priorities.
Track and improve key operational metrics, including deployment readiness, time to commissioning, system performance, issue resolution, customer satisfaction, and team utilization.
Promote a strong culture of safety, accountability, technical excellence, professionalism, and continuous improvement.
Develop a global operating model that accounts for regional hiring, travel, training, logistics, customer support, and local operating requirements.
Represent Field AI professionally with customer engineers, site leaders, executives, technology partners, and other stakeholders.
Maintain sufficient hands-on familiarity with Field AI’s technology and deployment processes to provide credible technical guidance and leadership in the field.
Travel to customer locations as needed to support critical deployments, coach team members, and strengthen customer relationships.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in robotics, engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Significant experience in field applications engineering, robotics deployment, systems integration, technical operations, or a comparable customer-facing engineering function.
Demonstrated experience leading, developing and managing technical field teams.
Experience building or scaling field operations across multiple customers, sites, or geographic regions.
Strong understanding of complex hardware and software systems, ideally involving robotics, autonomous systems, industrial automation, technical infrastructure or other deployed advanced technology.
Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent deployments and balance customer urgency, technical complexity, staffing constraints, and business priorities.
Strong troubleshooting and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to lead teams through ambiguous and high-pressure field situations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, frontline operators, customer executives, and internal leadership.
Strong organizational and operational discipline, including experience developing processes, documentation, training programs, and performance metrics.
Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally as business needs require.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience deploying robotic or autonomous systems in challenging, complex environments.
Experience supporting customers in industries such as energy, manufacturing, construction, mining, agriculture, logistics, aerospace, defense, or infrastructure.
Familiarity with Linux, networking, sensors, robotic hardware, autonomy software, and system-level diagnostics.
Experience managing distributed or international technical teams.
Experience operating within a high-growth technology company where products and processes are evolving rapidly.
Knowledge of industrial site safety, commissioning practices, and customer acceptance procedures.
Experience supporting the transition from early-stage pilots and demonstrations to repeatable, production-scale deployments.
Why Join Field AI?
Join a high-growth robotics company bringing advanced autonomous technology into some of the world’s most challenging operational environments. You will have the opportunity to build a globally important function, develop a world-class field engineering team, and directly influence how Field AI’s technology is deployed and supported at scale.
This is a highly visible leadership role with meaningful impact across our customers, products, and organization. You will work alongside exceptional engineers and industry leaders while helping shape the operating model that brings the next generation of robotics into the real world.

Field Services Technician

Conduct routine and incident maintenance for our Robot Fleet.

Report on critical team metrics such as mean time to repair and first contact resolution rate.

Local to Chicago, IL and able to travel within designated region (all expenses paid).

Comfortable with basic command line tools.
Ability to become vendor credentialed with partner hospitals.
3+ years of work experience with commercially available products.
Technical experience necessary to troubleshoot complex robotic systems.
Ability to execute high quality work without supervision in the field.
Strong work ethic, organizational and communication skills.
Must be a US citizen or permanent resident with work authorization.
Benefits:
Experience working with some of the leading experts in robotics
Potential to radically change the future of healthcare
Insurance including medical, dental, and vision
401K
Paid Time Off

Description
Amazon's Frontier AI & Robotics (FAR) team is building advanced robotic systems that will transform autonomous operations. Our mission is to push the boundaries of what's possible in robotics, developing next-generation hardware platforms that operate in complex, real-world environments.
FAR is seeking a Robotics Maintenance Specialist who will own day-to-day maintenance, repair, and operational readiness of our robotic hardware platforms, test systems, and lab infrastructure. This hands-on role focuses on keeping FAR's robotic platforms running at peak performance through predictive and preventive maintenance, expert troubleshooting, custom fabrication, and building team capability through mentorship and knowledge sharing. You'll work directly with engineers and researchers who design and build cutting-edge robotic systems, ensuring maximum hardware availability so the team can iterate fast without interruption.
This role may serve as an individual contributor or a technical lead/supervisor depending on the candidate's experience and aspirations. Candidates with team leadership experience may supervise and direct a team of contract maintenance technicians.
Key job responsibilities
Maintenance, Fabrication & Repair
- Maintain, troubleshoot, and improve a diverse fleet of robotic and electromechanical systems, including manipulators, mobile robots, and autonomous vehicle subsystems
- Design, build, and improve custom electrical harnesses, cable assemblies, and robotic modifications with emphasis on proper cable routing, strain relief, and system reliability
- Replace and repair electrical components (motor drivers, relays, sensors, power distribution) and mechanical components (bearings, gears, actuators, drivetrain assemblies, end-effectors)
- Troubleshoot and repair control systems including PLCs, motor controllers, embedded electronics, and sensor arrays; read and interpret electrical, mechanical, and pneumatic schematics
- Develop and execute preventive and corrective maintenance processes, SOPs, and maintenance plans for robotic systems
- Develop and implement failure-tracking systems to capture robotic failures, identify trends, perform root-cause analysis, and proactively reduce recurring issues
- Coordinate with robotics vendors for technical support, repairs, and replacement strategies; oversee vendor repairs while maintaining direct involvement in critical repairs
- Track spare-parts needs and maintain inventory records; coordinate with supply chain to ensure adequate stock levels for critical components
Lab, Fleet & Researcher Support
- Develop and manage robot fleet check-in/check-out processes to maximize equipment utilization and ensure researchers have access to operational robots
- Maintain laboratory and testing environments in a clean, organized, safe, and ready-to-use condition; maintain and calibrate test fixtures and measurement equipment
- Coordinate the setup, configuration, and deployment of high-value robotic assets; support lab reconfiguration, hardware integration, and prototype bring-up activities
- Serve as the primary maintenance point of contact for researchers, interns, and project teams; establish strong communication to understand requirements and develop practical solutions
- Review incoming requests, define scope and execution plans, establish timelines, and provide hands-on technical support to minimize equipment-related delays
Team Coordination & Continuous Improvement
- Supervise and direct a team of maintenance technicians, including defining daily and weekly priorities, assigning work, and ensuring alignment with project objectives
- Develop project plans, coordinate people, equipment, materials, and logistics; monitor progress, identify risks, and drive issues to resolution
- Cross-train technicians on common robotic failures, troubleshooting methodologies, and maintenance best practices; author and refine training documentation
- Analyze maintenance and failure data to identify improvement opportunities; partner with engineering teams to drive design changes that improve reliability
- Identify recurring hardware failures and develop standardized troubleshooting procedures and SOPs
- Build strong working relationships with researchers, technicians, project managers, engineering teams, and external vendors
- Continuously improve maintenance processes, lab operations, and documentation to support a rapidly changing research environment
Basic Qualifications
- 3+ years of conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures experience
- Associate's degree in Mechatronics, Robotics, Electrical Technology, or related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and experience)
- 3+ years of maintenance experience in robotics, autonomous systems, advanced manufacturing/technology, or R&D lab environments, including hands-on mechanical and electrical repair of complex electromechanical systems
- Proficiency reading and troubleshooting electrical and mechanical schematics
- Hands-on experience with motors, actuators, sensors, control systems, and diagnostic equipment
Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in a technical field
- 5+ years of maintenance experience, including direct experience maintaining robotic systems (industrial robots, mobile platforms, manipulators, or autonomous vehicles)
- Experience supervising or directing a team of maintenance technicians or skilled trades workers
- Hands-on experience designing and building custom electrical harnesses, cable assemblies, or robotic modifications
- PLC programming or configuration experience; familiarity with ROS, embedded Linux, or robotic middleware systems

About Dexterity
At Dexterity, we believe robots can positively transform the world. Our breakthrough technology frees people to do the creative, inspiring, problem-solving jobs that humans do best by enabling robots to handle repetitive and physically difficult work.

We’re starting with warehouse automation, where the need for smarter, more resilient supply chains impacts millions of lives and businesses around the world. Dexterity's full-stack robotics systems pick, move, pack, and collaborate with human-like skill, awareness, and learning capabilities. Our systems are software-driven and hardware-agnostic and have already picked over 15 million goods in production. And did we mention we’re customer-obsessed? Every decision, large and small, is driven by one question – how can we empower our customers with robots to do more than they thought was possible?

Dexterity is one of the fastest-growing companies in robotics, backed by world-class investors such as Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Obvious Ventures. We’re a diverse and multidisciplinary team with a culture built on passion, trust, and dedication. Come join Dexterity and help make intelligent robots a reality! At Dexterity, we believe robots can positively transform the world. Our breakthrough technology frees people to do the creative, inspiring, problem-solving jobs that humans do best by enabling robots to handle repetitive and physically difficult work.

About the Role
As a Forward Deployed Engineer you are the front line leading Dexterity's robots into new opportunities. You will work to bridge any gaps between Dexterity's standard product and the particular challenges of new customer engagements or new market segments. Your mission is to bring new applications online in the field and demonstrate all the operational metrics necessary to rapidly unlock fleet-wide scaling at each new customer opportunity.

This role is ideal for engineers with a passion for developing robotic solutions that operate in the real world at scale. This role requires broad, systems level understanding of the full robotic tech stack, both software and hardware. You will be expected to do system level performance analysis and drive system level solutions through hands on engineering, partnering with other teams across Dexterity, third party partners and the customer.


Physical & Work Environment:
Location: Redwood City, CA. Office desk-based tasks and lab-floor testing.
This position requires frequent travel to customer locations, with typically 50% of time spent on-site.
On-site assignments will involve warehouse conditions (temperature variations, industrial noise) and prolonged standing or walks.

Core Outcomes:
New Solution Introduction: Ensure successful pilot outcomes by driving new solution operations in the field, resolving early issues, meeting customer KPIs, and preparing the solution to scale rapidly post pilot.
High Quality and Rapid Resolution: Drive fixes and improvements based on field experience with proper methodologies to provide traceability, change management and eliminate repeat occurrences.
Operational Excellence: Release solutions that are ready to scale. Solutions should meet operator expectations for ease of use, up time and operator:robot ratio.
Customer Trust: Become the named technical point-of-contact for one or more strategic sites.
Engineering Feedback Loop: Develop new integrations, robotic skills and capabilities to meet new customer challenges. Extend and improve methodologies to incorporate field learning into the core platform capabilities towards the goal of general robot intelligence.
Deliver actionable bug reports and reproducible cases that accelerate root-cause analysis.
Field Enablement: Develop new tooling, documentation and provide guidance to application services teams at pilot and production sites. Collect and curate information in a way to drive automation of the support system.
Tooling & Observability:Develop proficiency and leverage internal platforms such as Portal, Foxglove, Kibana, ArgoCD, and Grafana for system analysis. Enhance observability and visualization to provide better insight to system behavior, particularly as new skills, capabilities and use cases are added.

Key Responsibilities:
Drive System Performance Improvement in the Field — The real world always presents subtle new challenges to intelligent systems. Your primary goal will be to translate field operations experience into better systems, improved learning and enhanced robot skills to optimize top line performance as robot deployments scale.
Diagnose & Resolve Incidents — Analyse logs, telemetry, SQL/NoSQL data, and container metrics to pinpoint failures; reproduce issues in staging; craft work-arounds or scripted hot-fixes; document in ticketing system (Jira/Zendesk).
Proactive Monitoring — Tune alerting rules, dashboards, and anomaly-detection models; perform trend analysis to track system performance towards KPI targets.
Field Presence — Embed on customer site during go-live, major upgrades, or chronic issue hunts. Understand what flies under the radar and how to surface it automatically through the observability stack.
Knowledge & Automation — Write SOPs, runbooks, and self-service articles; contribute to CLI tools and diagnostic scripts in Python/Bash; mentor TAC on new failure modes.
Continuous Improvement Projects — Partner with Product and Engineering on feature hardening, performance tuning, and reliability improvement.
Own and execute NPI software commissioning at customer sites, including tooling setup, system testing, and calibration.

Core Skills & Experience:
BS or MS in Computer Science, Robotics or a related discipline, or relevant experience.
Proficient in Python or C++, with experience implementing a large project or product feature.
Aptitude for Hands-On Work in Physical-AI Environments — must be willing work across the full breadth of the robot stack from sensors to software.
Data-driven Mindset, ability to instrument, query, and visualize telemetry to inform decisions.
Familiarity with support tools and observability platforms (e.g., Grafana, Kibana, Foxglove, ArgoCD).
Strong analytical and debugging skills; experience parsing logs and telemetry data.
Clear Communication — translate technical findings into customer-friendly language and crisp bug reports.
Self-starter mindset with a willingness to take ownership in ambiguous environments
Bias for Action — sense of urgency in production environments; willingness to “own the ticket” until closure.

Nice-to-Have, Role-Specific Strengths:
Experience supporting AI/ML inference platforms (model drift, retraining pipelines).
System-level Troubleshooting across Linux, networking (TCP/IP, VLANs, VPNs), containers (Docker/K8s), and cloud services (AWS/GCP/Azure).
Familiarity with message queues & real-time data buses ( RESTAPI).
Exposure to industrial automation or warehouse management systems.
Knowledge of CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions, ArgoCD) and feature-flag rollouts.
Basic understanding of robot kinematics and perception pipelines to converse with Product Support colleagues.

Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline (e.g., Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Robotics) or Computer Science — with demonstrable coding skills and a solid grounding in computer-science fundamentals. Equivalent practical experience is welcome.
2+ years in a SaaS, DevOps, Site Reliability, or Application Support role handling customer-facing production systems.
Comfortable working extended hours, on-site or on-call rotations for high-severity incidents.

Equal Opportunity Employer: We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

About Nimble
Nimble
is a robotics and AI company building end-to-end autonomous logistics to enable fast, efficient, and sustainable commerce. We’re developing generalized robot intelligence and building general-purpose logistics robots, the first in the world capable of performing all core warehouse functions.
Our mission is to empower and inspire mankind to accomplish legendary feats by inventing robots that liberate us from the menial.
Our long-term vision is to invent the Autonomous Supply Chain – everything from the inside of factories and warehouses to your front door – using next-gen intelligent robotics to deliver faster, more efficient, and more sustainable commerce.
We were founded from the AI labs at Stanford and Carnegie Mellon. We’re backed by the World’s most prestigious investors as well as AI and robotics legends like
Marc Raibert
(Founder of Boston Dynamics),
Fei-Fei Li
(Chief Scientist of AI at Google, Director of Stanford’s AI lab), and
Sebastian Thrun
(Founder of Google X, Waymo, Kitty Hawk, and Udacity)!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e3XPfrlkO7s
Nimble's Core Values:
1) Be relentlessly resourceful -
Find a way to make the impossible, possible. Do whatever it takes.
2) Be legendary -
Be the best at whatever it is that you do. Leave your mark. Motivate and inspire others.
3) Be humble -
Leave your ego behind. Have a growth mindset. Learn and improve yourself every day.
4) Be dependable -
Take ownership and deliver. Be loyal to your team and Nimble's mission.
About the Role
Nimble Robotics is seeking an experienced Maintenance Technician for an e-commerce fulfillment facility. Under general supervision, the technician performs critical corrective and preventive maintenance on mechanical equipment, material handling equipment, automated equipment, tools, buildings and grounds. This is a maintenance and repair position that is crucial in the daily operations of the fulfillment center.
Responsibilities
Work with management and lead technicians to prioritize daily tasks and assignments.
Effect repairs on machines, tools, building infrastructure, and other grounds equipment and resources.
Inspect, evaluate, and repair a variety of mechanical equipment.
Regularly uses assigned software to enter work done on work orders, and to track daily tasks & assignments.
Communicate with team members on site and abroad to gather necessary information for accurate repairs.
Maintain accurate records of work performed, parts used, and time taken for tasks.
Read and interpret specifications, diagrams, manuals and other documentation such as standard operating procedures created by engineering and management.
Confer with staff to determine equipment problems; suggest methods of minimizing such problems in an operational setting.
Help to maintain inventory levels of supplies, tools, and replacement parts. Working with management and distribution to ensure stock is replaced in a timely manner.
Follow appropriate safety procedures and work to applicable codes and guidelines, including making recommendations for improvements.
Attend training and safety sessions as assigned.
Basic Qualifications
Equivalent to graduation from high school and three years of experience in the maintenance and repair of a variety of equipment, structures, and facilities such as found in similar industrial settings
Read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Write reports, correspondence and procedures.
Effectively respond to questions from staff, other departments’ managers, and technical representatives.
Must be able to use computer systems including but are not limited to: Google Suite, Slack, Microsoft Visual Studio, command prompts, Click Up, and other various software applications.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form. Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to recognize, mitigate, and correct unsafe conditions.
Ability to interact with others (co-workers, supervisors, subordinates) in a professional manner; to accept constructive criticism from supervisors, equals, and subordinates; to work as a team member or independently as needed; to prioritize assignments and meet deadlines; to prevent personal problems from adversely impacting your work or that of others around you; to arrive at work as scheduled and to work the shift hours as scheduled.
Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability, fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations
Additional Requirements
Regularly required to use hand tools, to reach with hands and arms into tight spaces, and to talk or hear in person or on the telephone or radio
Hearing is frequently required for equipment operation analysis
Required to work and walk at elevated heights, using fall protection equipment.
Frequently required to stand, walk, sit, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl to access necessary equipment.
Occasionally required to smell, using odors to determine process or equipment problems.
Regularly lift and/or move up to 20 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 40 pounds, and occasionally be required to lift and/or move more than 50 pounds.
Close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Ability to work on-call/stand-by, overtime, weekends and holidays as needed
Work location is in a warehouse environment with variable temperature including cold, heat and humidity
Exposure to moving mechanical parts; fumes or airborne particles; occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; manufacturing conditions; heat; risk of electric shock; and vibration
Compensation
$40-$45/hr
Culture
We embrace challenges and strive to make the impossible possible each day. We’re not in this to do what’s easy or to be mediocre. We want to create something legendary and leave our mark on the world. We’re ambitious, we’re gritty, we’re humble and we’re relentlessly resourceful in pursuit of our goals. If this sounds like you then you might be a great fit!

ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Forward Deployed Robotics Engineer, you'll serve as the first line of technical defense for our growing fleet of robotic systems deployed across warehouse and external data-collection environments. Our diverse robot fleet—including both static and mobile systems—performs complex manipulation and sensing tasks in real-world settings. When issues arise, you'll be the first responder: analyzing field tickets, reproducing issues, gathering diagnostic data, and driving resolution to ensure maximum fleet uptime.



Key Responsibilities

- Primary Robot Fleet Issue Technical Triage Point: Manage incoming fleet issue ticket queue, prioritize based on fleet-wide implications and operational goals, and triage as hardware, software, or operational issue.

- Fast-Paced Operations: Handle quick turnaround expectations while maintaining diagnostic quality

- On-Site Diagnostics: Perform physical inspections and functional tests at robot stations to verify issue reproduction

- Data Analysis: Analyze telemetry, sensor data, and logs to form and test hypotheses about root causes

 - Failure Analysis: Execute technically sound Failure Analysis / Root Cause Analysis procedures

- Cross-Team Collaboration: Partner with hardware and software teams to reproduce and resolve complex issues

- Pattern Recognition: Identify recurring issues across the fleet and surface reliability insights for design improvements

- Documentation: Maintain clear, traceable documentation for every diagnostic and escalation event

- Metrics & Reporting: Track and report issue trends and fleet health metrics to leadership

- Process Improvement: Collaborate with team lead to develop and maintain diagnostic procedures and troubleshooting guides



Required Competencies & Skills

- Education: B.S. in Robotics, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or equivalent experience

- Hardware Knowledge: Proficiency debugging electromechanical systems including actuators, PCBs, cameras, wiring harnesses, and communication hardware

- Software Knowledge: Experience with log parsing and basic scripting for diagnostics (Python or Bash)

fields.full_description:
1. 以公司产品为核心，协助销售部门进行售前售中售后技术支持；
2. 负责对客户进行产品软硬件培训（硬件操作、软件使用以及二次开发等），完成设备交付；
3. 负责设备交付后的技术答疑、故障诊断处理、安排售后维修等工作；
4. 基于日常培训内容、整理已知问题解决办法，总结形成文档、视频，形成、完善产品知识库；
5. 整理产品问题、客户需求，形成合理的研发需求反馈给研发/产品经理，促进产品完善、升级；
6. 负责样机及售后备用机仓库管理，建立售后机器管理流程。负责制定售后标准化服务流程，并完成过程管控；
7. 售前技术部分工作内容：负责机器人巡检、监控集成项目需求调研，充分与销售人员、客户沟通交流，对需求进行挖掘和引导，输出解决方案，进行客户现场踏勘、需求分析、技术方案编制；负责与客户进行技术交流，技术方案讲解，机器人演示等工作。
